quotes.text: But there is another side of this, too, where we can’t blindly accept the good without also recognizing the potential bad. And just like every other technology out there, there are going to be malicious actors who are going to look to leverage these capabilities for their own end.
While generative AI has not introduced any fundamentally new risks to this election cycle, it has exacerbated those in the foreign influence operation and disinformation space and the cyber domain.

We have already seen this play out and fail. DC politicians are trying to continue to gut Medicaid, all while giving AI companies like Elon Musk's Grok the power to determine whether seniors get the healthcare they need. AND they want to make it so Musk would make money if healthcare is denied?

Absolutely not.

AI is transforming our country at a rate our current representatives just can’t keep up with. We have seen this story play out with social media companies before. Left unregulated and unchecked, corporations will continue to exploit our weak regulations at the expense of safety, security, and American jobs. We need leaders in Congress willing to put guardrails on this technology.

You shouldn’t allow an AI model to teach someone how to build a chemical or biological weapon, to build a bomb. These are things that should be common sense and aren’t political. Regulating AI shouldn’t be a partisan issue. It’s a public safety and service issue… I promise to lead the charge on regulating AI companies so we don’t suffer, and instead we see it be used as a force for good to do things like cure cancer and reverse climate change.

If you actually care about our troops @lawler4ny, maybe instead of posting a fake AI image of our servicemembers you could stop this spiraling President who doesn’t know what he’s doing getting us into a war with no objective and no way out. https://t.co/XEj0mVdQ2B

It was great to be at the @OssiningChamber Candidate Forum last night, which centered on the challenges small businesses are facing right now. Thank you to Hudson Valley Books for Humanity for hosting and all you do in our community!

It was an incredible turnout, and I loved getting to talk with so many of you afterward about everything from how hard it is for small businesses to afford healthcare, to AI ethics and accountability, to taking on corruption in Washington.

As we gear up for the primary, I am grateful for conversations like these and ready to fight for our small businesses and our communities here at home.

Last week I had the opportunity to join the @OssiningChamber, where people raised real concerns about what the future of AI will look like and whether they will benefit from it.

AI has the potential to help cure diseases, improve the quality and efficiency of healthcare, develop technologies to reverse the impacts of climate change, and help small businesses compete with companies ten times their size. But there are real concerns about public safety, misinformation, cyber threats, job displacement, and a lack of accountability from major tech companies that develop and deploy these systems.

As your representative in Congress, I will ensure AI works for the people – by passing clear data privacy laws, hold Data Centers accountable to guarantee they pay their fair share through binding agreements that protect residents from utility rate hikes and harmful impacts to our water supply, investing in community colleges and job retraining programs so workers can thrive in a changing economy, and demanding full transparency and human oversight.
If a data center is built in a way where there is a net-positive for the community, I support it. If it is a net-negative, then I do not. That should be our standard.

I know America can both lead the world, beat China and our adversaries in this space, and also do it the right way. But I think this goes back to getting the right people in Congress who know how to do that.

Shout out to the @RoCoYoungDems for taking the time to meet with me this week! From rising housing costs to ensuring good paying jobs to regulating AI, our federal government is failing to set up younger generations for success.

Our young people are our future, and it’s amazing to see so many teenagers and young adults getting into the arena to defend our democracy and fight for our communities.

AI poses a very real threat to the safety and security of the American people, and it’s long past time that Congress took action to regulate it. But Mike Lawler is standing in the way, because he’s looking out for his trillionaire backer Elon Musk.

Last year, Mike Lawler voted to ban states from regulating AI for 10 years. We cannot afford to wait a decade to enact guardrails that should already be put in place.

We need members of Congress who actually understand how to regulate AI and ensure it doesn’t pose a threat to our national security. After serving at the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, that’s the exact expertise I will bring to Washington.

It's no surprise that Elon Musk has spent millions to keep his puppet Mike Lawler in office.

Musk is the operator of the largest data center in the world, and Mike cast the deciding vote to give data center operators $80 billion in tax breaks, while voting to ban states from regulating data centers and AI operations.

Mike is serving his corporate, special interest, and trillionaire backers. As your member of Congress, I will serve you.

Mike Lawler’s disastrous record includes:
- Voting to ban states from regulating AI for 10 years.
- Voting to give data center developers $80 billion in tax breaks + voting to make it easier to build them.

As your member of Congress, I will:
- Enact guardrails on AI to ensure it doesn’t pose a threat to our national security.
- Take on Mike Lawler’s Big Tech and trillionaire backers to prevent these data center developers from exploiting our communities, harming our environment, and jacking up our utility rates.

I do believe the federal government has a role to ensure the safety and security of the people, and that means regulating AI, a technology we cannot afford to get wrong. Look, we've screwed up with social media, and children are literally paying the consequence.

I think if data centers are being built, they very clearly need to meet two thresholds. One, the local community has to support it, and two, they must be built in such a way where it is a net positive for that community. That means that they're not passing utility bills off to the local families.
I support a moratorium because right now we're watching as local communities are being exploited by these data center developers.
